title: Four Billion Tiny Flies Migrate to Britain Every Year
subject: hoverfly

scenes.text: Up to four billion animals migrate across the English Channel every year. You've never noticed.
They aren't birds. They're hoverflies, and they wait for favorable winds before taking off.
Radar tracked them flying as high as 1,000 meters, riding tailwinds for hundreds of kilometers in a day.
Why bother? Their larvae eat up to ten trillion aphids, and the adults pollinate billions of flowers.
In autumn they fly back. About a billion more return than arrived, roughly 28 tons of flies.
So next time a fly hovers over a flower, it may have just crossed a sea.
